la:verb:redeo.gloss: to go, move, turn or come back; turn around, return, revert, reappear, recur; to home
senses: to go, move, turn or come back; turn around, return, revert, reappear, recur; to home
to be brought or reduced to; arrive at, reach, attain
la:verb:redeo.html:
rĕd-ĕo, ĭi, ĭtum, īre (lengthened form of the
pres. redīnunt, Enn. ap. Müll.; cf.: obinunt, ferinunt, nequinunt, solinunt, for obeunt, feriunt, nequeunt, solent; and danit, danunt, for dat, dant; rare fut. redies, , and ; cf. ; ), v. n.
To go or come back; to turn back, re turn, turn around (freq. and class.; syn revertor).
Lit.
Of persons.
Absol.: bene re gestā salvus redeo,; : velletne me redire,: et non nisi revocaretis, rediturus fuerim,.—
With ex and abl.: erus alter ex Alide rediit,: e provinciā,: ex illis contionibus domum,.—
With ab and abl.: a portu,: a portā,: a foro,; ; cf.: a foro do mum,; : ab re divinā,: a cenā,: a Caesare,: a nobis,: ab Africā,: a flumine, et saep.—
With abl. alone: Thebis,: Cariā,: rure,; ; ; 8; : colle,: exsilio,: opsonatu,; ; : suburbanā aede,. — (ε) With adv. of place: unde,; : inde domum,: hinc, inde, unde, etc.,; ; — (ζ) With adv. of time or manner: eum rediturum actutum,; : pascua haud tarde redientia,: tardius,: mature,: retro,; ; .— (η) With in and acc.: in patriam,; ; : in urbem,; Drak. N. cr.: in castra,: in senatum rursus,; cf. joined with retro,; ; ; ; : veram in viam,; cf.: in rectam semitam,; and, in the same sense, simply in viam,; : in proelium,to renew,: serus in caelum redeas,: in gyrum, et saep. — (θ) With ad and acc.: ad navem,: ad parentes denuo,; so, ad aliquem,; ; ; ; : ad quos,: ad castra, Auct. B. Hisp. 25; cf.: se rediturum ad penates et in patriam,.— (ι) With acc. alone: Syracusas,: Romam ; : domum,; ; ; ; ; ; : Cirtam,: Babyloniam,; cf. (poet.): his laeti rediere duces loca amoena piorum,.— (κ) With adv. of direction, etc.: huc, illuc,; ; ; ; : isto,: intro,; ; : quo,.— (λ) With acc. of distance: ite viam, Vet. Form. ap. : itque reditque viam,.— (μ) Impers. pass.: dum stas, reditum oportuit,: ad arbitrum reditur,: manerent indutiae, dum ab illo rediri posset,: ut Romam reditum est,; ; .—(ν) With inf.: saepe redit patrios ascendere perdita muros,: hirundo reditura cibos immittere nidis, Montan. ap. .—
Of things: astra ad idem, unde profecta sunt,; cf.: sol in sua signa,: totidem redeuntia solis Lumina viderunt,: redeuntis cornua lunae,: adverso redierunt carbasa vento,: Eurus reditura vela tenebat,: flumen in eandem partem, ex quā venerat, redit,; cf.: amnes In fontes suos,: ille qui in se redit orbis,: redeunt jam gramina campis Arboribusque comae,; cf.: arboribus frondes,.—
Trop., to go or come back, to return: aspersisti aquam, Jam rediit animus,; so, animus,; : mens,: et mens et rediit verus in ora color,: spiritus et vita redit bonis ducibus,: suum redit ingenium,: memoria redit,: redit animo ille latus clavus, etc.,: in pristinum

statum, Gaes. B. G. 7, 54: in statum antiquum rediit res,; cf.: reditum in vestram dicionem,: cum Alcumenā antiquam in gratiam,: cum suis inimicissimis in gratiam,; id. Fragm. ap. ; ; ; cf.: se numquam cum matre in gratiam redisse, had never been reconciled, i. e. had never been at variance, ; and simply in gratiam,; ; cf.: in concordiam,: in amicitiam alicujus,: in fidem alicujus,: nunc demum in memoriam redeo,I recollect, call to mind,; so, in memoriam mortuorum,; ; ; cf.: in memoriam cum aliquo,: in corda redeunt tumultus,: vere calor redit ossibus,: redit agricolis labor actus in orbem,: rursum ad ingenium redit,he returns to his natural bent,; so, ad ingenium,: ad se atque ad mores suos,: ad se,; but redire ad se signifies also, to come to one's self, i. e. to recover one's senses, ; cf. ; ; ; cf.: ex somno vix ad se,: donec discussis redeunt erroribus ad se,: ad sanitatem,; cf.: reverto: in veram rediit faciem solitumque nitorem, returned to his true form (of Apollo), ; cf.: in annos Quos egit, rediit,i. e. he resumed his youth, (for which: reformatus primos in annos,): in juvenem,: in fastos,to go back to them,: quamvis redeant in aurum Tempora priscum,: in causas malorum,to appear again as the cause of misfortunes,: maturos iterum est questa redire dies, (3, 10), 12; so of times and events which recur periodically: annus,; ; : ne rediret Saeculum Pyrrhae,: Nonae Decembres,: iterum sollemnia, (3, 31), 1 al.—Impers. pass.: tum exuto justitio reditum ad munia,.—

In partic., in speaking, thinking, or writing.
Of the speaker, to go back, return to a former subject, to recur to it: mitte ista, atque ad rem redi, etc.,: quid si redeo ad illos,: sed de hoc alias: nunc redeo ad augurem,; so, ad Scipionem,: ad me,: ad fabulas,: ad illa prima,fin.: sed ad illum redeo,: ad inceptum,: illuc, unde abii, redeo,; ; : longius evectus sum, sed redeo ad propositum,; cf.: digredi a re et redire ad propositum,: ab illo impetu ad rationem redit, et saep. —Comically: nunc in Epidamnum pedibus redeundum'st mihi,.—
Of the subject: res redit,comes up again,; cf.: redit de integro haec oratio,.—
(With the idea of ire predominating; cf.: recido, redigo).
To come in as revenue, income; to arise, proceed (cf. provenio): tribus tantis illi minus redit,: ut ex eodem semine aliubi cum decimo redeat, aliubi cum quintodecimo,: possentne fructus pro impensā ac labore redire,: ex pecore redeunt ter ducena Parmensi,: pecunia publica, quae ex metallis redibat,: ex quā regione quinquaginta talenta quotannis redibant,: e modio redire sextarios quattuor siliginis,; et saep.—
To come to, be brought or reduced to; to arrive at, reach, attain a thing; constr. usually with ad; very rarely with in or an adv. of place: pilis omissis ad gladios redierunt,betook themselves to their swords,; cf.: ad manus reditur, Auct. B. Afr. 18, 4: Caesar opinione trium legionum dejectus, ad duas redierat,was brought down, reduced,: collis leniter fastigatus paulatim ad planitiem redibat, sank or sloped down, descended, : ejus morte ea ad me lege redierunt bona, have descended to me, ; so, ad hos lege hereditas,: quorum (principum) ad arbitrium judiciumque summa omnium rerum consiliorumque redeat,: summa imperii, rerum ad aliquem,; ; : regnum ad aliquem,: res ad interregnum,: mihi ad rastros res, (with redigat ad inopiam): ut ad pauca redeam,i. e. to cut the story short,; : aut haec bona in tabulas publicas nulla redierunt, aut si redierunt, etc., have not reached, i. e. are not registered upon, : Germania in septentrionem ingenti flexu redit,trends towards the north,: in eum res rediit jam locum, Ut sit necesse,; : in nubem Ossa redit,rises to,: Venus, quam penes amantūm summa summarum redit,falls to her lot, pertains to her,: quod si eo meae fortunae redeunt, ut, etc.,come to that,; so, adeo res,; ; ; : omnia verba huc redeunt,come to, amount to this,; cf.: incommoditas huc omnis,.

la:verb:redeundus.gloss: which is to be returned etc
senses: which is to be returned etc

la:noun:reditus.gloss: a returning, turning back, going back; return
senses: a returning, turning back, going back; return
a return, revenue, income, proceeds, yield, output, profit
la:noun:reditus.html:
rĕdĭtus, ūs, m.
redeo
.
A returning, return (freq. and class.).
Lit.: noster itus, reditus,: reditu (returning) vel potius reversione (turning back) meā laetatus, : inter profectionem reditumque L. Sullae,: aliquem reditu arcere,: spe omni reditūs incisā,: Romanis reditu interclusis,; Auct. B. Alex. 20, 5: excludi reditu,: ne metum reditūs sui barbaris tolleret,: maturum reditum pollicitus,: unde tibi reditum Parcae Rupere,: pascitur in vestrum reditum votiva juvenca,: votum pro reditu simulant, et saep.: qui vero Narbone reditus?: animis reditum in caelum patere,: in locum,; ; ; ; : reditus in patriam ad parentes,: in nemora,; : Romam,: domum,home,: ad aliquem,: ad vada,.—In plur., ; ; ; : promittere inanes reditus,: patent reditus populo,—Of the revolution of the heavenly bodies: homines populariter annum tantummodo solis, id est unius astri, reditu metiuntur,; cf. in plur., . —
Trop., a returning, return: reditus in gratiam cum inimicis,: gratiae,: reditus ad rem ... ad propositum,.—
(Acc. to redeo, II. 1.) A return, revenue, income, proceeds (not in Cic.; late Lat.; also redditus,; cf.: vectigalia, proventus); in sing.: omnisque ejus pecuniae reditus constabat,; : in reditu esse,to make returns,: decrescente reditu, id ; ; ; .— In plur., ; Wolf. N. cr.; 41; ; ; ; .

senses: to give up, hand over, deliver, render, provide, assign
to surrender, relinquish, deliver, yield, resign
to give or pay back; take revenge for, punish, inflict vengeance for
to repeat, declare, report, narrate, recite, rehearse, express
to make something look in a certain way, make or cause a thing to be or appear something or somehow, render
la:verb:reddo.html:
red-do, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3 (old
fut. reddibo = reddam, ; , acc. to ; id. Fragm. ap. ; pass. reddibitur, ), v. a.
Lit., to give back, return, restore (freq. and class.; syn. restituo): reddere est quod debeas ei cujus est volenti dare,: ut mihi pallam reddat, quam dudum dedi,; ; cf.: potes nunc mutuam drachmam dare mihi unam, quam cras reddam tibi?; so corresp. to dare,; : quid si reddatur illi, unde empta est,; ; et saep.; cf. the foll.: ea, quae utenda acceperis, majore mensurā, si modo possis, jubet reddere Hesiodus,; so corresp. to accipere,; ; ; : accipe quod nunquam reddas mihi,; ; et saep.: si quid ab omnibus conceditur, id reddo ac remitto,I give it back and renounce it,: Th. Redde argentum aut virginem. Ph. Quod argentum, quam tu virginem, me reposcis? : ut (virginem) suis Restituam ac reddam,; so with restituere,; cf.: reddere alias tegulas, i. e. restituere,: obsides, Naev. ap. ; so ; ; 6, 12: captivos,; : ho mines,: corpora (mor tuorum),; cf. : equos,; : suum cuique,: hereditatem mulieri,: sive paribus paria redduntur,i. e. are set against, opposed to,: nosmet ipsos nobis reddidistis,: redditus Cyri solio Phraates,: reddas incolumem, precor,: ut te reddat natis carisque,: redditus terris Daedalus,; cf.: patriis aris,: oculis nostris,: tenebris,: sed jam urbi votisque publicis redditus,: ex magnā desperatione saluti redditus,: quin tu primum salutem reddis, quam dedi,: operam da, opera reddibitur tibi,; so : cum duo genera liberalitatis sint, unum dandi beneficii, alterum reddendi, demus nec ne, in nostrā potestate est; non reddere viro bono non licet,; so ; and cf. : redde his libertatem,; so, Lyciis libertatem ademit, Rhodiis reddidit,: patriam,: sibi ereptum honorem,: conspectum, al.: se ipse convivio reddidit,betook himself again to the banquet, returned,: quae belua reddit se catenis,: se reddidit astris,; so, lux terris,: se iterum in arma,.—
Poet., with inf.: sua monstra profundo Reddidit habere Jovi,.—
Absol. (rare and poet.), of a river: sic modo conbibitur, modo Redditur ingens Erasinus,is swallowed up ... reappears,. —
Transf.
To give up, hand over, deliver, impart, assign; to yield, render, give, grant, bestow, pay, surrender, relinquish, resign (syn.: trado, refero): Cincius eam mihi abs te epistulam reddidit, quam tu dederas,; so, litteras (alicui),; : litteras a te mihi reddidit stator tuus,; ; ; ; ; cf. mandata,: pretium alicui pro benefactis ejus,: hoccine pretii,; cf.: praemia debita (along with persolvere grates),: cetera praemia (with dare),: primos honores,: gratiam alicui (for the usual referre gratiam),: reddunt ova columbae,: obligatam Jovi dapem,: o fortunata mors, quae naturae debita, pro patriā est potissimum reddita,; cf.: vitam naturae reddendam,; so, vitam. : debitum naturae morbo,i. e. to die by disease,: lucem,: ultimum spiritum,; cf. ; fin.; 2, 87, 2: animam caelo,fin.; cf. animas (with moriuntur),: hanc animam, vacuas in auras,: caute vota reddunto,to pay, offer, render,; so, vota,; : tura Lari,: liba deae,: fumantia exta,; ; cf.: graves poenas,i. e. to suffer,: promissa viro,: tibi ego rationem reddam?will render an account,; so, rationem,; ; v. ratio: animam a pulmonibus respirare et reddere,to give off, exhale,; cf.: ut tibiae sonum reddunt,give forth,; so, sonum,; ; ; : vocem,; ; (with mugiit); : stridorem,: murmura,: flammam, et saep.; so, alvum,: bilem,: sanguinem,to vomit, (just before: sanguinem rejecit): urinam,: calculum,: catulum partu,; cf. so of parturition,; : fructum, quem reddunt praedia,yield, produce,; ; ; ; ; cf. ; : generi nostro haec reddita est benignitas,is imparted to,; cf.: nulla quies est

Reddita corporibus primis, . — Hence, poet., redditum esse, in gen., = factum esse, esse: una superstitio, superis quae reddita divis,which is given, belongs to the gods,: quibus et color et sapor una reddita sunt cum odore,; cf. Munro ad loc.; ; Orell. ad : neque iis petentibus jus redditur,is dispensed, granted,: alicui jus,; cf.: alicui testimonium reddere industriae,: quod reliquum vitae virium, id ferro potissimum reddere volebant,to yield, sacrifice,: quibus ille pro meritis ... jura legesque reddiderat,had conferred upon it the power of self-jurisdiction,; cf Drak.: Lanuvinis sacra sua reddita,: conubia,to bestow, grant,: peccatis veniam,: nomina facto vera,to call by the right name,.— Hence,

Jurid. t. t.: judicium,to appoint, grant, fix the time for a trial,; ; ; : jus,to administer justice, pronounce sentence,; 13, 51; ; ; et saep.—
To give up, yield, abandon to one that which has not been taken away, but only threatened or in danger: Thermitanis urbem, agros legesque suas reddere, ( = relinquere, , § 88): Orestis leges suae redditae,left undisturbed,; (cf. restituere); 29, 21, 7.—
To give back, pay back; hence, to take revenge for, punish, inflict vengeance for: per eum stare quominus accepta ad Cannas redderetur hosti clades,: reddidit hosti cladem,: redditaque aequa Cannensi clades,.—
To give back in speech or writing, i. e.
To translate, render (syn.: converto, transfero): cum ea, quae legeram Graece, Latine redderem,: verbum pro verbo,: verbo verbum,; cf. .—
To repeat, declare, report, narrate, recite, rehearse (freq. in Quint.): ut quae secum commentatus esset, ea sine scripto verbis iisdem redderet, quibus cogitasset,; cf. : sive paria (verba) paribus redduntur, sive opponuntur contraria,: reddere quae restant,: tertium actum de pastionibus,: nomina per ordinem audita,: causas corruptae eloquentiae,: quid cuique vendidissent,: dictata,to repeat, rehearse,; : carmen,to recite, deliver,: cum talia reddidit hospes,; : causam,: insigne exemplum suo loco,.—
To answer, reply (poet.): veras audire et reddere voces,; : Aeneas contra cui talia reddit,; 2, 323: auditis ille haec placido sic reddidit ore, et saep.; cf. responsa,: responsum,; ; .—
To give back or render a thing according to its nature or qualities; to represent, imitate, express, resemble (poet. and in post - Aug. prose): quas hominum reddunt facies,: faciem locorum,; : lux aemula vultum Reddidit,gave back, reflected,: formam alicujus,: et qui te nomine reddet Silvius Aeneas,; cf.: jam Phoebe toto fratrem cum redderet orbe,: paternam elegantiam in loquendo,; ; cf.: odorem croci saporemque,i. e. to smell and taste like saffron,: imaginem quandam uvae,: flammam excellentis purpurae et odorem maris,: Apelleā redditus arte Mentor,.—
To give back, return a thing changed in some respect: senem illum Tibi dedo ulteriorem lepide ut lenitum reddas,; cf.: quas tu sapienter mihi reddidisti opiparas opera tua,.— Hence, in gen.,
To make or cause a thing to be or appear something or somehow; to render (very freq. and class.; cf.: facio, redigo): reddam ego te ex ferā fame mansuetem,; : eam (servitutem) lenem reddere,: tutiorem et opulentiorem vitam reddere, : haec itinera infesta reddiderat,: aliquem insignem,: obscuraque moto Reddita forma lacu est,dimmed by the disturbance of the water,: homines ex feris et immanibus mites reddidit et mansuetos,: omnes Catilinas Acidinos postea reddidit, has made all the Catilines seem to be Acidini, i. e. patriots, in comparison with himself, : aliquid perfectum,: aliquid effectum,to accomplish,; ; : omne transactum,: actum,: dictum ac factum,.— With ut and subj.: hic reddes omnia Quae sunt certa ei consilia incerta ut sient,.— Pass. = fieri scripsit fasciculum illum epistularum totum sibi aquā madidum redditum esse, ; ; : per sudorem corpus tantum imbecillius redditur,; cf. ; ; ; ; prooem.; .

la:verb:redigo.gloss: to drive, lead, or bring back
senses: to drive, lead, or bring back
to call in, collect, raise, receive
to reduce to a certain state
la:verb:redigo.html:
rĕd-ĭgo, ēgi, actum, 3, v. a.
ago
.
To drive, lead, or bring back (syn. reduco).
Lit.: (Sol) Disjectos redegit equos,: si materiem nostram collegerit aetas Post obitum, rursumque redegerit, ut sita nunc est,bring it back, restore it to its present condition,: filia parva duas redigebat rupe capellas,: tauros in gregem,; cf.: in sua rura boves,: oppidani (hostem) fusum fugatumque in castra redigunt,: hostium equitatum in castra,: turbam ferro in hostes,: aliquem Capuam,: aliquem in exsilium,. —
Trop.: rem ad pristinam belli rationem redegit,: annum neglegentia conturbatum ad pristinam rationem,: disciplinam militarem ad priscos mores,: aliquid ad ultimam sui generis formam speciemque, : omnia redegit in singulas rationes praeceptionis,: aliquem in concordiam,: vos in gratiam,: tu, qui ais, redige in memoriam,recall it to my mind,: in memoriam,; : (poëtae) formidine fustis Ad bene dicendum delectandumque redacti,brought back, reduced,.—Far more freq.,
(With the idea of agere predominant; cf. recido and redeo, II.) To get together, call in, collect, raise, receive, take a sum of money or the like by selling, etc.: cum omnem pecuniam ex aerario exhausissetis, ex vectigalibus redegissetis, ab omnibus regibus coëgissetis,; cf.: pecuniam ex bonis patriis,; and simply pecuniam,; : omne argentum tibi,to scrape together,: bona vendit, pecuniam redigit ... pecunia, quam ex Agonidis bonis redegisset,; cf. : quod omnis frumenti copia decumarum nomine penes istum esset redacta, etc.,: fructus, (after colere agros); 22, 1, 46; cf.: pars maxima (praedae) ad quaestorem redacta est,: fructus ad eum,: quicquid captum ex hostibus est, vendidit Fabius, consul, ac redegit in publicum,paid it into the public treasury,: venditum sub hastā in aerarium,: (patres) victi irā vetuere reddi (bona regia), vetuere in publicum redigi,; cf.: praedam in fiscum,: aliquid in commune,.—
To bring or reduce a thing to any condition, circumstance, etc.; to make or render it so and so (cf. reddo); constr. with in (so most freq.), ad, sub, an adv. of place, absol., or with a double acc.
With in: viros in servitutem,: Aeduos in servitutem,: in pristinam sortem servitutis,: vidulum in potestatem alicujus,: civitatem in potestatem,; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf.: civitatem in dicionem potestatemque populi Romani,: aliquos in dicionem,; : gentes in dicionem hujus imperii,: Arvernos in provinciam,to reduce to a province,; fin.; cf.: partem Britanniae, etc., in formam provinciae,; ; ; ; ; ; : in formulam provinciae,: in formam praefecturae,: in id redactus sum loci, Ut, etc.,; cf.: republicā in tranquillum redactā,; and: mentem in veros timores,: si hoc genus (pecuniarum) in unum redigatur,be brought into one mass,: dispositio est, per quam illa, quae invenimus, in ordinem redigimus,reduce to order,; cf.: arbores in ordinem certaque intervalla,; but: ut veteres grammatici auctores alios in ordinem redegerint, alios omnino exemerint numero, brought, admitted into the rank of classics (cf. Gr. ἐγκρίνειν; opp. numero eximere = ἐκκρίνειν): libertinos in equestrem ordinem,; ; ; for which: redigere aliquem (poëtam) in numerum,; also,to lower, degrade,; v. ordo; cf. Liv. ap. P.; : quod prosa scriptum redigere in quaedam versiculorum genera,: in hanc consuetudinem memoriā exercitatione redigendā,: servos, in dominium nostrum,: in nihilum redigam te, et non eris,: in cinerem, Pet. 2, 6: provinciam in solitudinem, Lact. de Ira Dei, 5, 4.—
With ad: aliquem ad inopiam redigere,to reduce to poverty,: aliquem ad incitas,; : genus id ad interitum,; Cic. ap. ; cf.: prope ad internecionem gente ac nomine Nerviorum redacto,: ad nihilum redigere,: victoriam ad vanum et irritum,to render empty and useless,: cf.:

spem ad irritum, : aliquid ante dubium ad certum,to render certain,: carnes excrescentes ad aequalitatem, (shortly afterwards reducunt); cf.: cicatrices ad planum,: aliquem ad desperationem,; et saep.: redegit se ad pallium et crepidas,.—

With sub: Galliam sub populi Romani imperium,: Corcyram sub imperium Atheniensium,: barbaros sub jus dicionemque,: incolas ejus insulae sub potestatem Atheniensium,; fin.; ; : totam Italiam sub se,: GENTES SVB IMPERIVM,.—
With adv. of place: eo redigis me, ut, etc.,: eo, ut,: hem! Quo redactus sum!.—(ε) Absol.: ut credam, redigunt animum mihi argumenta, Att. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 516 Rib.): ut ejus animum retundam, redigam, ut, quo se vortat, nesciat, bring it down, so that, etc., ; .— (ζ) With double acc., to make or render a thing something (very rare; more freq. reddere): quae facilia ex difficillimis animi magnitudo redegerat,: (Ubios) Suevi multo humiliores infirmioresque redegerunt,fin.; .—
In designations of number, etc., pregn., to bring within a number or extent; to lessen, diminish, reduce: familiam jam ad paucos redactam paene ab interitu vindicasti,; cf.: redigere omnis fere in quadrum numerumque sententias,: hosce ipsos (libros octo) utiliter ad sex libros redegit Diophanes,reduced, abridged,: ex hominum milibus LX. vix ad D.... sese redactos esse dixerunt,: ad semuncias redacta,: judicia ad duo genera judicum redegit,; : non ad numerum redigar duorum,: quod si comminuas vilem redigatur ad assem,: ne res ad nilum redigantur funditus omnes,; ; cf. : rem maximam redigere ad minimum,.

la:verb:redimo.html:
rĕd-ĭmo, ēmi, emptum, 3, v. a.
emo
.
To buy back, repurchase (freq. and class.; syn.: recupero, reparo).
In gen.: eam (domum) non minoris, quam emit Antonius, redimet,: neque adeo hasce emi mihi — illi redemi rursum,: aut emendum sibi quod non habebat, aut redimendum quod habebat,: de fundo redimendo,: orabo, ut mihi pallam reddat, quam dudum dedi, Aliam illi redimam meliorem,will buy in return,; ; cf. .—
In partic., to buy back, ransom, release, redeem a prisoner, slave, etc.: Li. Tu redimes me, si me hostes interceperint? De. Redimam, ; : ut is homo redimatur illi,; cf. : captos, captivos ab hoste, a praedonibus, etc.,; ; cf.: haec benignitas, redimi e servitute captos,; : servi in publicum redempti ac manumissi,ransomed, liberated at public cost,: me raptum pugnā pretiove redemptum Mandere humo,; ; . — Hence,
In gen., to buy off from any thing; to set free, release, rescue: aliquem a piratis publicā civitatium pecuniā,: pecuniā se a judicibus, palam redemerat,; cf.: se ab inquisitoribus pecuniā,: se a Gallis auro,: se a cane,: se ab invidiā fortunae,: aliquem suo sanguine ab Acheronte,; cf.: fratrem Pollux alternā morte redemit,: corpus (sc. a morbo),: redimite armis civitatem, quam auro majores vestri redemerunt,; : so, redemit Dominus Jacob,; Pet. 1, 18 et saep. —
To buy up.
Lit.
In gen. (rare): statim redemi fundos omnes, qui patroni mei fuerant,: essedum sumptuose fabricatum,: libros suppressos,.—
Of persons, to hire, bribe: auditores conducti et redempti,; so, plausor redemptus,: tutor aut curator redemptus,: aemuli corrupti ac redempti,.— More freq. and class.,
In partic., a mercant. and jurid. t. t., to take or undertake by contract; to hire, farm, etc.: Dumnorigem portoria reliquaque omnia Aeduorum vectigalia parvo pretio redempta habere,; Müll.; cf.: picarias de censoribus,: opus,: istum eripiendum,, § 31: vestimenta texenda vel insulam, vel navem fabricandam,: litem,to undertake,.— Esp., in law, t. t., to undertake the risk of a suit for a consideration (which was held dishonorable; opp. to the authorized stipulation of a fee): litem te redemisse contra bonos mores,; cf. also: redimit eventum litium majoris pecuniae praemio contra bonos mores (procurator),: qui alios actionum suarum redimunt exactores,i. e. who engage persons to undertake their suits in their own names,; so ; cf., respecting redimere litem, Mühlenbruch, Die Lehre von der Cession, p. 362 sq.—
Trop., to buy, purchase.
To gain, acquire, obtain, procure any thing desirable: ut ab eo (praetore) servorum sceleris conjurationisque damnatorum vita vel ipso carnifice internuncio redimeretur,: ego vitam omnium civium ... quinque hominum amentium ac perditorum poenā redemi,: non vitam liberum sed mortis celeritatem pretio, : sepeliendi potestatem pretio,: pacem sibi sempiternam,: pacem Ariovisti ne obsidibus quidem datis,: pacem ab aliquo,: omnium gratiam atque amicitiam ejus morte,: militum voluntates largitione,: primo tantummodo belli moram,: neve auro redimat jus triste sepulcri,: mutuam dissimulationem mali,: quidquid homines vel vitā aestimant vel morte redimunt,; .—
To buy off, i. e. to ward off, obviate, avert an evil: quam (acerbitatem) ego a re publicā meis privatis et domesticis incommodis libentissime redemissem,: haec vero, quae vel vitā redimi recte possunt, aestimare pecuniā non queo,: qui se uno quaestu decumarum omnia sua pericula redempturum esse dicebat,, § 49: metum virgarum pretio,, § 117: ignominiam assiduo labore,: bellum ab Illyriis pactā mercede redimere,; cf. bella,; ; : si mea mors redimenda tuā esset,; cf.: nec te pugnantem tua forma redemit,: qui delatorem redemit,has bought off, hushed up,.—
To pay for; to make amends, atone, compensate for a wrong: flagitium aut facinus redimere,: multa desidiae crimina morte, Ruhnk.: nullam congiario culpam,; cf. simply culpam, Planc. ap. : vitium auctore (sc. Jove),: sua perjuria per nostram poenam,.—
Of one's word or promise, to redeem, keep: verba sua,.

la:verb:reduco.gloss: to lead, draw, bring or conduct back; bring or accompany home
senses: to lead, draw, bring or conduct back; bring or accompany home
to withdraw, cause to retreat, draw back, remove
to bring back, restore, recall, revive, rescue, replace; reform
to bring, produce or get out a quantity of
to bring, make or reduce to a certain condition or quality
to recall to the mind, remember, remind
to subjugate (to bring under the yoke)
la:verb:reduco.html:
rĕ-dūco, xi, ctum, 3 (rēduco or redduco, ; ; ; old
imp. redduce, ), v. a.
To lead or bring back, to conduct back (very freq. and class.; syn. redigo).
Lit.
In gen.
Of living objects: reducam te ubi fuisti,: hunc ex Alide huc reducimus,; cf.: aliquem ex errore in viam,: aliquem de exsilio,; ; cf.: ab exsilio,: socios a morte,: Silenium ad parentes,; so, ad aliquem,; ; ; fin.; cf.: a pastu vitulos ad tecta,: reduci in carcerem,: in Italiam,: reducere uxorem,to take again to wife, marry again,; ; ; 4, 4, 12 sq. al.; ; ; ; cf.: uxorem in matrimonium,: regem,to restore to the throne, to reinstate,; ; ; (v. reductio): possum excitare multos reductos testes liberalitatis tuae,i. e. who have been brought back by your generosity,; cf.: cum in Italiam reductus existimabor, Pomp. ap. . —
With inanimate objects, to draw back, bring back: (falces) tormentis introrsus reducebant,: reliquas munitiones ab eā fossā pedes CCCC. reduxit,; cf. turres,fin.: calculum, ap. : in jaculando bracchia,: sinum dextrā usque ad lumbos,: ad pectora remos,; : clipeum,to draw back,: gladium (opp. eduxit),: auras naribus,: furcillas hibernatum in tecta,. —Poet.: solem reducit,; so, diem (Aurora),: lucem (Aurora),: noctem die labente (Phoebus),: aestatem,: hiemes,: febrim,: somnum (cantus),: umbram,to make the shadow move backwards,.—
In partic.
Reducere aliquem domum (opp. deducere), to conduct or accompany one home, : (P. Scipio) cum senatu dimisso domum reductus ad vesperum est a patribus conscriptis,; cf. ; cf.: quos Elea domum reducit Palma,.—So, without domum: in ludum (puellulam) ducere et reducere,: aliquem ad suam villam,: bene comitati per forum reducuntur,: quantā reduci Regulus solet turbā,: assurgi, deduci, reduci, .—
In milit. lang., to draw off, withdraw troops: vastatis omnibus eorum agris Caesar exercitum reduxit,: legiones reduci jussit,; so, exercitum (copias, legiones suas, etc.),; ; ; ; ; ; sq.: suos incolumes,; ; : legiones ex Britanniā,: a munitionibus,: ab oppugnatione,fin.: in castra,fin.; 1, 50; 2, 9; 4, 34 et saep.: in hiberna,: in Treviros, etc.,; 7, 9 fin.; : intra fossam,; cf.: ab radicibus collis intra munitiones, —Absol. (like duco and educo): instituit reducere,to march back, and 8.—
To recall to the stage a player: a magno Pompeio magni theatri dedicatione anus pro miraculo deducta,.—
Trop., to bring back, restore, replace: ad divitias,: animum aegrotum ad misericordiam,: aliquem in gratiam,; : in gratiam cum aliquo,; ; ; cf.: ut Caesarem et Pompeium perfidiā hominum distractos rursus in pristinam concordiam reducas, Balbus ap. , A, 1: aliquem ad officium sanitatemque,: propinquum ad officium,: judices ad justitiam,: legiones veterem ad morem,: meque ipse reduco A contemplatu,withdraw myself,: verba paulum declinata ad veritatem,: judicatio est ad eum statum reducenda,: reducere in memoriam quibus rationibus unam quamque partem confirmāris,; cf.: in memoriam gravissimi luctūs,: dolorem in animum judicantium,: vocem in quendam sonum aequabilem,: verborum facilitatem in altum,: haec benignā in sedem vice,: tu spem reducis mentibus anxiis Viresque,: diem et convivia mente re duxit,has recalled to mind,: vel instituere vel reducere ejusmodi exemplum, etc.,to introduce again, restore,; so, habitum vestitumque pristinum,: morem transvectionis post longam intercapedinem,. — To bring back, restore to the right path: scire est liberum Ingenium et animum, quo vis illos tu die Redducas,.—
After the Aug. period, sometimes with the idea of ducere predominating, for the usual redigere (q. v. II.). *
To bring or get out, to produce a certain quantity: LX. pondo panis e modio (milii) reducunt,.—
To bring, make, reduce to some shape, quality, condition, etc. (rare; usually redigere): aliquid in formam,: faecem in summum,to bring up, raise,: excrescentes carnes in ulceribus ad aequalitatem efficacissime reducunt (just before, redigit),: cicatrices ad colorem,: corpus sensim ad maciem,: ulcera ac scabiem jumentorum ad pilum,.— Hence, rĕ-ductus, a, um, P. a., drawn back, withdrawn; of place, retired, remote, distant, lonely.
Lit.: inque sinus scindit sese unda reductos,; ; so, vallis,; ; .—
Trop.: virtus est medium vitiorum et utrimque reductum,from either extreme,.— In painting: alia eminentiora, alia reductiora fecerunt,less prominent,: producta et reducta (bona), a transl. of the Gr. προηγμένα καὶ ἀποπροηγμένα of the Stoics, things to be preferred and those to be deferred, .— Sup. and adv. do not occur.

la:adj:redux.gloss: that leads or brings back, that returns
senses: that leads or brings back, that returns
that is led or brought back (from slavery, imprisonment, from a distance, etc.), come back, returned, that has returned
la:adj:redux.html:
rĕdux (rēdux, ; id. Capt. 5, 1, 2), dŭcis (abl. reduce, :
reduci,), adj.
reduco
.
Act., that leads or brings back (mostly as an epithet of Jupiter and of Fortuna, in the poets and in inscrr.): et sua det reduci vir meus arma Jovi,; Sabin. Ep. 1, 78; : hic ubi Fortunae reducis fulgentia late Templa nitent,; ; ; sq.; 1776; 3096; 4083: reduces choreae,i. e. that accompany home,.— Of a human being only in the foll. passage: eo pervenimus, unde, nisi te reduce, nulli ad penates suos iter est,.—
Pass., that is led or brought back (from slavery, imprisonment, from a distance, etc.), come back, returned (freq. and class.): facere aliquem reducem,to bring back,; cf. ; 3, 5, 28; 5, 1, 2; 11; ; : ab Orco in lucem,: quid me reducem esse voluistis? (i. e. from exile), : victores triumphantes domos reduces sistatis,; cf.: reduces in patriam ad parentes ad conjuges ac liberos facere,: navi reduce,: caesar exercitusque,: reduces socios,; : gratari aliquem reducem, et saep.: (elephanti) non ante reduces ad agmen,: carina,: reduces habenas,; of the phœnix after being burned: reducisque parans exordia formae,.

la:verb:redoleo.gloss: to emit a scent or odor
senses: to emit a scent or odor
to be redolent or smell of or like
la:verb:redoleo.html:
rĕd-ŏlĕo, ŭi, ēre, v. a. and n.,
to emit a scent, diffuse an odor; to smell of or like, be redolent of any thing.
Act.
Lit.: vinum redolens,smelling of wine,: unguenta,: thymum,: illa tuas redolent medicamina mensas,; : foetorem acoremve,: delicias,.—
Trop.: orationes redolentes antiquitatem,: doctrinam exercitationemque paene puerilem,: servitutem paternam,: nihil,. —
Neutr.
Lit., absol: quod fracta magis redolere videntur Omnia,; so : in patulis redolentia mala canistris, al.—With gen.: fila Tarentini redolentia porri edisti,. — With abl.: redolent thymo fragrantia mella,; : mella thymi redolentia flore,; ; —
Trop.: mihi quidem ex illius orationibus redolere ipsae Athenae videntur,; Orell. N. cr.: praefectus urbis, cui nescio quid redoluerat, a conventu se abstinuit, who had got scent of something, II.
la:verb:redoleo.inflection: ŭi, ēre, v. a. and n.

la:verb:redimio.gloss: to encircle, gird, crown (with a garland)
senses: to encircle, gird, crown (with a garland)
la:verb:redimio.html:
rĕdĭmĭo, ĭi, ītum, 4 (
imperf. redimibat, ; ), v. a.
etym. dub.
, to bind round, wreathe round, encircle, gird, crown, etc. (mostly poet.; syn.: cingo, circumdo).
In the verb finit.: caput atque umeros plexis redimire coronis,: cui tempora vittā,: mitrā capillos,: crinem corymbis,: chelyn,: frontem coronā,: sertis redimiri jubebis et rosā?: lauro tabellas,; cf.: fastigium aedis tintinnabulis,: hortum floribus, Col. poët. 10, 286. —Poet.: nec sic innumeros arcu mutante colores Incipiens redimitur hiems,is girt round, environed,.—
In part. perf.: sertis redimiti,; cf.: redimitus coronis,: anguineo redimita capillo Frons,: frons corymbis,: frons regium in morem,; ; cf.: domus floridis corollis,: navigia variarum coronarum genere,; ; v. Sillig ad h. l.: loca silvis, girtround, surrounded, ; cf.: Naxos Aegaeo ponto,.— Absol.: missile,the wreathed thyrsus,: cervix,.— In a poet. construction: redimitus tempora lauro, quercu, mitrā, etc.,; ; ; ; ; ; ; cf.: caput harundine redimitus,

la:verb:reducto.html:
rĕducto, āre, v. freq. a.
reduco
; in milit. lang.,
to withdraw, draw back: exercitum,

la:noun:redimiculum.html:
rĕdĭmīcŭlum, i (collat. form rĕdĭ-mīcŭla, ae, f., late Lat., ), n.
redimio
,
a band.
Lit.
A fillet, necklace, chaplet, frontlet, etc., : habent redimicula mitrae,; ; : qui longa domi redimicula sumunt frontibus,; cf. Müll.: redimicula sunt quibus mitra adligatur,.—
A girdle: redimiculum est, quod succinctorium sive bracile nominamus, quod descendens per cervicem et a lateribus colli divisum utrarumque alarum sinus ambit atque hinc inde succingit, etc. Hunc vulgo brachilem quasi brachialem dicunt, quamvis nunc non bracchiorum sed renum sit cingulum,.— *
Trop., a bond, fetter, .

la:verb:redarguo.html:
rĕd-argŭo, ŭi, 3, v. a.,
to disprove, refute, confute, contradict (class.; syn.: refello, refuto).
With acc.: nosque ipsos redargui refellique patiamur,; so, aliquem,; ; opp. probare,; so, orationem (opp. convinci),: contraria,: crimen,: famosos libellos,. — Of abstr. subjects: improborum prosperitates redarguunt vim omnem deorum ac potestatem,: inconstantiam tuam,: advenit qui vestra dies muliebribus armis Verba redarguerit, will refute thy words, show them to be false, * .— *
With object-clause: audi rationem falsam quidem, sed quam redarguere falsam esse tu non queas,.—
With gen., to convict of, prove guilty of: nec sane magnum aliquid efficiemus, quod illos ignorantiae redarguemus,; cf.: redarguti a lege quasi transgressores,. —
Absol.: poterat autem inpune; quis enim redargueret?; .

la:noun:redundantia.html:
rĕdundantĭa, ae, f.
redundans
,
an overflowing, superfluity, excess. *
Lit.: aër crassus, qui non habet crebras redundantias,—
Trop., redundancy, excess, of language, feeling, etc.: illa pro Roscio juvenilis redundantia,: benignitatis,: carere redundantiā et egestate,.

la:noun:redemptor.html:
rĕdemptor, ōris, m.
id.
.
In all periods of the lang., one who undertakes a thing by way of contract; a contractor, undertaker, purveyor, farmer (syn. conductor); absol.: redemptor qui columnam illam de Cottā et de Torquato conduxerat faciendam,; so in lemm.; : redemptori tuo dimidium pecuniae curavi,; ; ; et saep.— With gen.: tutelae Capitolii,: pontis,one who farmed the tolls of a bridge,: vectigalium, et saep.; cf. Müll., and Becker, Antiq. 2, 1, p. 270 and 3, 2, p. 217.—
In jurid. Lat.: redemptor litis.
One who releases a debtor from a demand, by paying his creditor, —
One who, for a consideration, undertakes the risk of a suit (freq.), ; —
In eccl. Lat., the Redeemer (of the world from sin), ; ; ; et saep.

la:verb:reddo#2.html:
red-do, dĭdi, dĭtum, 3 (old
fut. reddibo = reddam, ; , acc. to ; id. Fragm. ap. ; pass. reddibitur, ), v. a.
Lit., to give back, return, restore (freq. and class.; syn. restituo): reddere est quod debeas ei cujus est volenti dare,: ut mihi pallam reddat, quam dudum dedi,; ; cf.: potes nunc mutuam drachmam dare mihi unam, quam cras reddam tibi?; so corresp. to dare,; : quid si reddatur illi, unde empta est,; ; et saep.; cf. the foll.: ea, quae utenda acceperis, majore mensurā, si modo possis, jubet reddere Hesiodus,; so corresp. to accipere,; ; ; : accipe quod nunquam reddas mihi,; ; et saep.: si quid ab omnibus conceditur, id reddo ac remitto,I give it back and renounce it,: Th. Redde argentum aut virginem. Ph. Quod argentum, quam tu virginem, me reposcis? : ut (virginem) suis Restituam ac reddam,; so with restituere,; cf.: reddere alias tegulas, i. e. restituere,: obsides, Naev. ap. ; so ; ; 6, 12: captivos,; : ho mines,: corpora (mor tuorum),; cf. : equos,; : suum cuique,: hereditatem mulieri,: sive paribus paria redduntur,i. e. are set against, opposed to,: nosmet ipsos nobis reddidistis,: redditus Cyri solio Phraates,: reddas incolumem, precor,: ut te reddat natis carisque,: redditus terris Daedalus,; cf.: patriis aris,: oculis nostris,: tenebris,: sed jam urbi votisque publicis redditus,: ex magnā desperatione saluti redditus,: quin tu primum salutem reddis, quam dedi,: operam da, opera reddibitur tibi,; so : cum duo genera liberalitatis sint, unum dandi beneficii, alterum reddendi, demus nec ne, in nostrā potestate est; non reddere viro bono non licet,; so ; and cf. : redde his libertatem,; so, Lyciis libertatem ademit, Rhodiis reddidit,: patriam,: sibi ereptum honorem,: conspectum, al.: se ipse convivio reddidit,betook himself again to the banquet, returned,: quae belua reddit se catenis,: se reddidit astris,; so, lux terris,: se iterum in arma,.—
Poet., with inf.: sua monstra profundo Reddidit habere Jovi,.—
Absol. (rare and poet.), of a river: sic modo conbibitur, modo Redditur ingens Erasinus,is swallowed up ... reappears,. —
Transf.
To give up, hand over, deliver, impart, assign; to yield, render, give, grant, bestow, pay, surrender, relinquish, resign (syn.: trado, refero): Cincius eam mihi abs te epistulam reddidit, quam tu dederas,; so, litteras (alicui),; : litteras a te mihi reddidit stator tuus,; ; ; ; ; cf. mandata,: pretium alicui pro benefactis ejus,: hoccine pretii,; cf.: praemia debita (along with persolvere grates),: cetera praemia (with dare),: primos honores,: gratiam alicui (for the usual referre gratiam),: reddunt ova columbae,: obligatam Jovi dapem,: o fortunata mors, quae naturae debita, pro patriā est potissimum reddita,; cf.: vitam naturae reddendam,; so, vitam. : debitum naturae morbo,i. e. to die by disease,: lucem,: ultimum spiritum,; cf. ; fin.; 2, 87, 2: animam caelo,fin.; cf. animas (with moriuntur),: hanc animam, vacuas in auras,: caute vota reddunto,to pay, offer, render,; so, vota,; : tura Lari,: liba deae,: fumantia exta,; ; cf.: graves poenas,i. e. to suffer,: promissa viro,: tibi ego rationem reddam?will render an account,; so, rationem,; ; v. ratio: animam a pulmonibus respirare et reddere,to give off, exhale,; cf.: ut tibiae sonum reddunt,give forth,; so, sonum,; ; ; : vocem,; ; (with mugiit); : stridorem,: murmura,: flammam, et saep.; so, alvum,: bilem,: sanguinem,to vomit, (just before: sanguinem rejecit): urinam,: calculum,: catulum partu,; cf. so of parturition,; : fructum, quem reddunt praedia,yield, produce,; ; ; ; ; cf. ; : generi nostro haec reddita est benignitas,is imparted to,; cf.: nulla quies est

Reddita corporibus primis, . — Hence, poet., redditum esse, in gen., = factum esse, esse: una superstitio, superis quae reddita divis,which is given, belongs to the gods,: quibus et color et sapor una reddita sunt cum odore,; cf. Munro ad loc.; ; Orell. ad : neque iis petentibus jus redditur,is dispensed, granted,: alicui jus,; cf.: alicui testimonium reddere industriae,: quod reliquum vitae virium, id ferro potissimum reddere volebant,to yield, sacrifice,: quibus ille pro meritis ... jura legesque reddiderat,had conferred upon it the power of self-jurisdiction,; cf Drak.: Lanuvinis sacra sua reddita,: conubia,to bestow, grant,: peccatis veniam,: nomina facto vera,to call by the right name,.— Hence,

Jurid. t. t.: judicium,to appoint, grant, fix the time for a trial,; ; ; : jus,to administer justice, pronounce sentence,; 13, 51; ; ; et saep.—
To give up, yield, abandon to one that which has not been taken away, but only threatened or in danger: Thermitanis urbem, agros legesque suas reddere, ( = relinquere, , § 88): Orestis leges suae redditae,left undisturbed,; (cf. restituere); 29, 21, 7.—
To give back, pay back; hence, to take revenge for, punish, inflict vengeance for: per eum stare quominus accepta ad Cannas redderetur hosti clades,: reddidit hosti cladem,: redditaque aequa Cannensi clades,.—
To give back in speech or writing, i. e.
To translate, render (syn.: converto, transfero): cum ea, quae legeram Graece, Latine redderem,: verbum pro verbo,: verbo verbum,; cf. .—
To repeat, declare, report, narrate, recite, rehearse (freq. in Quint.): ut quae secum commentatus esset, ea sine scripto verbis iisdem redderet, quibus cogitasset,; cf. : sive paria (verba) paribus redduntur, sive opponuntur contraria,: reddere quae restant,: tertium actum de pastionibus,: nomina per ordinem audita,: causas corruptae eloquentiae,: quid cuique vendidissent,: dictata,to repeat, rehearse,; : carmen,to recite, deliver,: cum talia reddidit hospes,; : causam,: insigne exemplum suo loco,.—
To answer, reply (poet.): veras audire et reddere voces,; : Aeneas contra cui talia reddit,; 2, 323: auditis ille haec placido sic reddidit ore, et saep.; cf. responsa,: responsum,; ; .—
To give back or render a thing according to its nature or qualities; to represent, imitate, express, resemble (poet. and in post - Aug. prose): quas hominum reddunt facies,: faciem locorum,; : lux aemula vultum Reddidit,gave back, reflected,: formam alicujus,: et qui te nomine reddet Silvius Aeneas,; cf.: jam Phoebe toto fratrem cum redderet orbe,: paternam elegantiam in loquendo,; ; cf.: odorem croci saporemque,i. e. to smell and taste like saffron,: imaginem quandam uvae,: flammam excellentis purpurae et odorem maris,: Apelleā redditus arte Mentor,.—
To give back, return a thing changed in some respect: senem illum Tibi dedo ulteriorem lepide ut lenitum reddas,; cf.: quas tu sapienter mihi reddidisti opiparas opera tua,.— Hence, in gen.,
To make or cause a thing to be or appear something or somehow; to render (very freq. and class.; cf.: facio, redigo): reddam ego te ex ferā fame mansuetem,; : eam (servitutem) lenem reddere,: tutiorem et opulentiorem vitam reddere, : haec itinera infesta reddiderat,: aliquem insignem,: obscuraque moto Reddita forma lacu est,dimmed by the disturbance of the water,: homines ex feris et immanibus mites reddidit et mansuetos,: omnes Catilinas Acidinos postea reddidit, has made all the Catilines seem to be Acidini, i. e. patriots, in comparison with himself, : aliquid perfectum,: aliquid effectum,to accomplish,; ; : omne transactum,: actum,: dictum ac factum,.— With ut and subj.: hic reddes omnia Quae sunt certa ei consilia incerta ut sient,.— Pass. = fieri scripsit fasciculum illum epistularum totum sibi aquā madidum redditum esse, ; ; : per sudorem corpus tantum imbecillius redditur,; cf. ; ; ; ; prooem.; .

rĕdemptĭo, ōnis, f.
redimo
.
A buying back, buying off; a releasing, ransoming, redemption: cum captivis redemptio negabatur,: ducis (capti),: puellae,: sacramenti, i. e. the purchase of one's military oath, i. e. of his discharge, Auct. B. Alex. 56, 4 (cf. : qui se pecuniā redemerunt).— Absol.: quia mercede pactā accesserat ad talem redemptionem, i. e. a releasing or release of the debtor from the demand, by paying the creditor, ; v. redemptor.—
A buying up of a court of justice, bribing: judicii,. — Plur. and absol.: reorum pactiones, redemptiones,.—
A farming of the revenue, .—
Esp. (eccl. Lat.), a release from sin or from its penalties, a rescuing from death, etc.: animae suae,; absol., .

la:verb:redintegro.gloss: to restore or renew, refresh or revive
senses: to restore or renew, refresh or revive
la:verb:redintegro.html:
rĕd-intĕgro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to make whole again; to restore, renew; to recruit, refresh (good prose; syn.: renovo, restauro, recreo): vide, quantis imbribus repente dejectis (di) solum molliant venasque fontium arentes redintegrent,: laetitiam (with renovare),: ut renovetur, non redintegretur oratio,be not repeated word for word,: interpretatio est, quae non idem redintegrat verbum,: ut deminutae copiae redintegrarentur,: soluto matrimonio ... redintegrato rursus matrimonio,: redintegratis viribus,: proelium,; so ; 2, 27; ; ; cf. bellum,: bellum alicui, Brut. ap. : dissensionem civilem,: pacem,: clamorem,; : luctum in castris,: memoriam,; : spem,; cf. animum,fin.: animos,: (columbae fastidientes) libero aëre redintegrentur,are recruited, refreshed,; cf. id : legentium animum,. — Absol.: iterum tum jucunditas in herbā redintegrabit (sc. pecus),.

la:verb:redamo.gloss: to requite love, to love back, to love in return, to return love for love
senses: to requite love, to love back, to love in return, to return love for love
la:verb:redamo.html:
rĕd-ămo, āre, v. a.,
to love back, love in return, return love for love (formed by Cic. after the Gr. ἀντιφιλεῖν): qui vel amare vel, ut ita dicam, redamare possit, Cic. Lae). 14, 49; also in late Lat.,; ; ; Leo M. Sern. 72; .

senses: to pour or spout forth or out; cause to pour out
la:verb:redundo.html:
red-undo, āvi, ātum, 1,
v. n.; of water, from being over full, to run back or over, to pour over, stream over, overflow (freq. and class.; a favorite word of Cic., esp. in trop. senses; not in Cæs., Verg., or Hor.; cf.: refluo, recurro).
Lit.: mare neque redundat unquam neque effunditur,: si lacus Albanus redundasset,; so, lacus,; cf. : redundantibus cloacis, Fragm. ap. ( Dietsch): Nilus campis redundat,; so, fons campis,; and: aqua gutture pleno,: cum pituita redundat aut bilis,; cf.: locos pituitosos et quasi redundantes,: sanguis in ora et oculos redundat,. —
Poet., in part. pass.: redundatus = redundans: amne redundatis fossa madebat aquis,; and for undans: (Boreae vis saeva) redundatas flumine cogit aquas, the swelling, surging waters (opp. aequato siccis aquilonibus Istro), .—
Transf.: redundare aliquā re, or absol., to be over full of, to overflow with any thing.
Of things: quae (crux) etiam nunc civis Romani sanguine redundat,is soaked with,; cf.: sanguine hostium Africa,; and : largus manat cruor: ora redundant Et patulae nares,.—
Of persons: hesternā cenā redundantes,. —
Trop., to flow forth in excess, superabound, redound, to be superfluous, redundant; to flow forth freely, to be copious, to abound: is (Molo) dedit operam, ut nimis redundantes nos juvenili quādam dicendi impunitate et licentiā reprimeret, et quasi extra ripas diffluentes coërceret,: ne aut non compleas verbis, quod proposueris, aut redundes,; cf.: Stesichorus redundat atque effunditur,: Asiatici oratores parum pressi et nimis redundantes,; ; cf. ; ; : hoc tempus omne post consulatum objecimus iis fluctibus, qui per nos a communi peste depulsi, in nosmet ipsos redundarunt,: quod redundabit de vestro frumentario quaestu,: quorum (vitiorum) ad amicos redundet infamia,: vitia Atheniensium in civitatem nostram, : si ex hoc beneficio nullum in me periculum redundavit,; cf.: servi, ad quos aliquantum etiam ex cottidianis sumptibus ac luxurie redundet,: in genus auctoris miseri fortuna redundat,: nationes, quae numero hominum ac multitudine ipsa poterant in provincias nostras redundare,: si haec in eum annum redundarint,: quod laudem adulescentis propinqui existimo etiam ad meum aliquem fructum redundare,to redound,; cf.: gaudeo tuā gloriā, cujus ad me pars aliqua redundat,: omnium quidem beneficiorum quae merentibus tribuuntur non ad ipsos gaudium magis quam ad similes redundat,; : nisi operum suorum ad se laudem, manubias ad patriam redundare maluisset,: ut gloria ejus ad ipsum redundaret,, ext. 4; Auct. B. Alex. 60, 2: animus per se multa desiderat, quae ad officium fructumve corporis non redundant,: ex rerum cognitione efflorescat et redundet oportet oratio,pour forth copiously, abundantly,: ex meo tenui vectigali . . . aliquid etiam redundabit,something will still remain,: non reus ex eā causā redundat Postumus,does not appear to be guilty,: hinc illae extraordinariae pecuniae redundarunt,have flowed, proceeded,; cf. , § 103: ne quid hoc parricidā civium interfecto, invidiae mihi in posteritatem redundaret, should redound to or fall upon me, . — *
Poet., with acc.: Vulturnus Raucis talia faucibus redundat,spouts forth,.—
Transf., to be present in excess; to be redundant, superabound; and: redundare aliquā re, to have an excess or redundancy of any thing: redundat aurum ac thesauri patent, Lucil. ap. : in quibus (definitionibus) neque abesse quicquam decet neque redundare,; cf.: ut neque in Antonio deesset hic ornatus orationis neque in Crasso redundaret,; : ut nulla (species) neque praetermittatur neque redundet,: munitus indicibus fuit, quorum hodie copia redundat,: splendidissimorum hominum multitudine,; cf.: redundante multitudine,: quod bonum mihi redundat,: quo posset urbs et accipere ex mari, quo egeret, et reddere, quo redundaret,: omnibus vel ornamentis vel praesidiis redundare,: tuus deus non digito uno redundat, sed capite, collo, cervicibus, etc.,: hominum multitudine,; cf. armis,: hi clientelis etiam exterarum nationum redundabant,: acerbissimo luctu redundaret ista victoria,: Curiana defensio tota redundavit hilaritate quādam et joco,.— Hence, rĕdundans, antis, P. a., overflowing, superfluous, excessive, redundant: amputatio et decussio redundantioris nitoris,.— Adv.: rĕdundanter, redundantly, superfluously, excessively, .— Comp., .

la:verb:redhibeo.gloss: to take, carry or give back, return
senses: to take, carry or give back, return
la:verb:redhibeo.html:
rĕd-hĭbĕo (rĕt-hĭb-), no
perf., ĭtum, 2, v. a.
habeo
, mercant. t. t., to take back a defective article purchased; hence, of the buyer, to carry, give back; of the seller, to receive back: redhibere est facere, ut rursus habeat venditor, quod habuerat, et quia reddendo id fiebat, idcirco redhibitio est appellata quasi redditio,; cf. the whole chapter,, De redhibitione, etc.: si malae emptae Forent, nobis istas redhibere haud liceret,to give back, return,; cf.: in mancipio vendendo dicendane vitia, quae nisi dixeris, redhibeatur mancipium jure civili,; and: (eunuchum) redhiberi posse quasi morbosum, etc.,; : (servus) redhibitus ob aliquod vitium,: rem,: dixit (sc. venditor) se (ancillam) redhibere, si non placeat, to take or receive back, (but in , the correct read. is reddibo; v. Ritschl ad h. l.).

la:adj:redivivus.html:
rĕdĭ-vīvus, a, um, adj.
v. re init.
.
That lives again (late Lat.; cf. recidivus): Christus,.—
Renewed, renovated, of old building-materials used as new: redivivus rudus (opp. novum),: unam columnam efficere ab integro novam, nullo lapide redivivo,. — Subst.: rĕdĭ-vīvum, i, n., old material used again in building: quasi quicquam redivivi ex opere illo tolleretur ac non totum opus ex redivivis constitueretur,; cf.: redivivum est ex vetusto renovatum, Müll.

rĕductĭo, ōnis, f.
reduco
,
a leading or bringing back; a restoring, restoration (very rare): quoniam senatūs consultum nullum exstat, quo reductio regis Alexandrini tibi adempta sit, * (shortly afterwards: ut per te restituatur et sine multitudine reducatur): per cujus (clipei) reductiones et demissiones, by the

raising and lowering of which,

la:noun:reduvia.html:
rĕdŭvĭa (rĕdĭvĭa), ae, f.
A hangnail on the finger: rediviam quidam, alii reluvium appellant, cum circa ungues cutis se resolvit, Müll.; cf. Paul. ex ib.; so, redivia, Titin. ib.: reduviae,; .— Prov.: cum capiti mederi debeam, reduviam curo,i. e. to be busy about trifles,. —
Transf., a remainder, remnant, fragment: escarum,: conchyliorum,.
